I am 76 years old and I have farmed this land in Shinyanga since I was a boy walking behind my father. This plot is big — more than 13 hectares — so my sons and their wives help me, and I must hire young men from the village for the clearing and weeding because my back is not strong anymore. I mix my crops together the way my father taught me, and I put cow dung on the fields near the homestead where my cattle sleep. I do not buy those white fertilizers from town — I never went to school, I cannot read the bags, and that money must pay the workers instead — and I use seed I kept from last harvest because I know it grows when the rains come.
